identity.symptom: synchronous watcher admission suspends on dynamic import

what: Manual source-watcher startup threw AsyncFiberError, blocking source and scaffold reload admission.
expected: startDevSourceWatcher must synchronously return its owned watcher handle after a manual session has started; CLI startup must retain lazy loading and session-scoped cleanup.
observed: A native SDK session served HTTP, but startDevSourceWatcher immediately threw because the effect it passed to runSync always awaited a dynamic import.
root_cause: startDevSourceWatcher in dev-watch.ts ran session.nativeEngine.watch synchronously. That effect in dev-session-engine.ts begins with ownedNativePromise importing dev-watch.js, which must suspend even when the module is cached. Effect.runSync correctly rejects suspended work.
fixed_by: Add a narrow internal watchWith operation that supplies the existing engine authorities and Scope to an already-loaded watcher effect. The synchronous facade uses it directly; the normal CLI watch effect continues importing lazily and then uses the same owner. Preserve the public watcher return type and supervisor API.

invariants: Watch worker and registrations share the acquired native session lifetime.
Ordinary and prepared CLI loading remains lazy and recovery preserves valid traffic.
Session shutdown joins workers and removes all owned processes and listeners.

reproduction: Run the complete package layer: both manual watcher and scaffold-reload tests fail with AsyncFiberError.
Run the isolated scaffold test: the session starts, then synchronous admission throws.
Add and run focused regression: initial /hello HTTP returns hello, then watcher creation fails.
Supply the already-loaded watcher effect through existing native capabilities and Scope.
Replay focused unit, native scaffold/source tests, complete package layer, and both literal bun dev CLI/HTTP matrices.
